core_obligations: Reduce to the structure assertion (proof lines 13013-13018): by uniqueness of left duals it suffices to show that F^bullet is locally strictly perfect; let G^bullet, eta, epsilon be a left dual and decompose eta = sum eta_n and epsilon = sum epsilon_n with eta_n : O -> F^n tensor G^{-n} and epsilon_n : G^{-n} tensor F^n -> O.

Split the duality termwise (proof lines 13019-13029): substituting the identities (1 tensor epsilon)(eta tensor 1) = id and (epsilon tensor 1)(1 tensor eta) = id gives (1 tensor epsilon_n)(eta_n tensor 1) = id_{F^n} and (epsilon_n tensor 1)(1 tensor eta_n) = id_{G^{-n}}, so G^{-n} is a left dual of F^n and the module-level lemma applies to each F^n.

Localise (proof lines 13030-13045): for U in C there is a covering {U_i -> U} over which only finitely many eta_n|_{U_i} are nonzero; replacing U by U_i and applying the module-level lemma makes only finitely many F^n|_U nonzero, and applying it once more gives a further covering over which each F^n|_Ui is a direct summand of a finite free module, so F^bullet is locally strictly perfect.
proof_roadmap: Use uniqueness of left duals to reduce to the local structure of F^bullet.
Split the unit and counit into their components, obtaining a termwise duality between F^n and G^{-n}.
Localise so that only finitely many components are nonzero and each term is a summand of a finite free module, giving local strict perfectness and hence the termwise description of the dual.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a complex of modules on a ringed site admitting a left dual in the monoidal category of complexes is locally strictly perfect, with the dual given termwise (statement lines 12999-13010). The proof (proof lines 13012-13045) decomposes the unit and counit of the duality into their components, which yields a termwise duality between F^n and G^{-n} so that the module-level description applies, and then localises so that only finitely many components are nonzero and each term becomes a direct summand of a finite free module. H2: one component decomposition followed by a localisation, written out.
